docs.title: Dotfiles - Quick Start
docs.text: Plain steps. Copy, paste, done. Details and the "why" are in Dotfiles reference.

docs.title: Which profile am I?
docs.text:
Answer one question: whose machine is this?

The machine is... Pick Mine (my own laptop / PC / Mac) rg-personal Mine to use, but not really mine (family PC, borrowed) rg-semi The company dev VDI rg-vdi The company laptop rg-work (only Lintalist) Shared with a colleague rg-collab Public / untrusted rg-public

Unsure? Pick the smaller one. You can change it later (below).

docs.title: New personal Windows laptop
docs.text:
1. Open PowerShell (Start → type PowerShell → Enter).

2. Install git and chezmoi:

winget install Git.Git twpayne.chezmoi

Close PowerShell, open it again.

3. Get my setup:

chezmoi init https://github.com/Buerostuff/dotfiles.git
  • A browser opens → log in to GitHub (account Buerostuff).
  • It asks Profile → type rg-personal → Enter.

4. Look before it changes anything:

chezmoi diff

Scroll with Space, quit with q. It only shows - nothing changes yet.

5. Apply:

chezmoi apply -v

This places all settings and installs the programs with winget. Takes a while. Some installers may ask "Allow changes?" → Yes.

At the end you may see a yellow list "Install by hand" (e.g. Lintalist). Download those from the shown link into C:\Install\Programs\<name>.

6. Make an SSH key for this laptop (to push later):

ssh-keygen -t ed25519 -C "personal-laptop"

Press Enter 3 times (or set a passphrase - remember it!).

Get-Content $HOME\.ssh\id_ed25519.pub | Set-Clipboard

GitHub → Settings → SSH keys → New SSH key → title "personal-laptop" → paste → Add.

Test:

ssh -T git@github.com

Shows Hi Buerostuff! → good.

7. Close and open the terminal. You should see the Starship prompt. Done.

docs.title: New Mac
docs.text:
1. Open Terminal (Cmd+Space → Terminal).

2. Install Homebrew (copy the line from https://brew.sh), then:

brew install git chezmoi

3–5. Same as Windows:

chezmoi init https://github.com/Buerostuff/dotfiles.git   # Profile: rg-personal
chezmoi diff
chezmoi apply -v

Windows-only things (Lintalist, VS Code paths, Windows Terminal) are skipped automatically.

6. SSH key:

ssh-keygen -t ed25519 -C "macbook"
pbcopy < ~/.ssh/id_ed25519.pub

Paste on GitHub like above. Test: ssh -T git@github.com.

docs.title: New company VDI
docs.text:
No admin here, so a few extra steps.

1. chezmoi: download the Windows zip from https://github.com/twpayne/chezmoi/releases (file chezmoi_..._windows_amd64.zip), unpack into C:\Install\Programs\chezmoi.

2. Put it on PATH:

[Environment]::SetEnvironmentVariable('Path',
  [Environment]::GetEnvironmentVariable('Path','User') + ';C:\Install\Programs\chezmoi',
  'User')

Close PowerShell, open it again. Check: chezmoi --version.

3. Get the repo and set up:

git clone https://github.com/Buerostuff/dotfiles.git C:\Install\_github\dotfiles
chezmoi init --source C:\Install\_github\dotfiles

Profile → rg-vdi.

4. Look, then apply:

chezmoi diff
chezmoi apply -v

On the VDI nothing gets downloaded - you get a yellow list of programs missing in C:\Install\Programs. Install those by hand (links are shown).

5. SSH (port 22 is blocked here): see Git SSH Setup, use the github_vdi alias. Test: ssh -T github_vdi.

6. New terminal → Starship prompt, dotnet --version shows 10.x. Done.

docs.title: New company laptop
docs.text:
winget install twpayne.chezmoi

New PowerShell, then:

chezmoi init https://github.com/Buerostuff/dotfiles.git   # Profile: rg-work
chezmoi apply -v

Only Lintalist settings come over. Install Lintalist by hand into C:\Install\Programs\lintalist64 (link is shown), then chezmoi apply once more.

docs.title: Every day - what do I do?
docs.text:
Nothing, mostly.

I... What happens / what I do change a setting (Starship, Terminal, Lintalist snippet, VS Code keys) Auto-saved and committed within an hour (on the next terminal start). A yellow line says so. see push when ready cd to the dotfiles repo → git push see new untracked ... say 'check all and sync' Tell the AI agent "check all and sync" → it asks what to add → I say yes → it commits → I push. see possible secret in ... Don't push. Open the file, remove the password, run Sync-Dotfiles. see repo has uncommitted changes I edited the repo by hand. Commit or undo it there. want my changes from another machine here chezmoi update

Where is the repo?

chezmoi cd      # opens a shell in the repo; type exit to leave

docs.title: Add a new config file to sync
docs.text:
chezmoi add ~/.config/sometool/config.toml

Then tell the agent "check all and sync" so it puts it in the right profile group. Or do it yourself: add it to .chezmoidata/dotfiles.yaml + .chezmoiignore.

docs.title: Add a program to install everywhere
docs.text:
Open .chezmoidata/packages.yaml in the repo, copy an entry, change it:

  - name: 7-Zip
    winget: 7zip.7zip          # find with: winget search 7zip
    brew: sevenzip             # find with: brew search 7zip (Mac/Linux)
    dir: 7-Zip                 # VDI folder name
    url: https://www.7-zip.org/download.html
    on: [rg-personal, rg-vdi]  # who gets it

Then:

chezmoi apply -v

Commit + push.

docs.title: Change my agent rules
docs.text:
chezmoi edit ~/.config/opencode/AGENTS.md
chezmoi apply

(Don't edit ~/.config/opencode/AGENTS.md directly - it gets overwritten.)

docs.title: Change the profile later
docs.text:
chezmoi init --prompt
chezmoi apply -v

docs.title: Stop syncing a file
docs.text:
chezmoi forget ~/.config/sometool/config.toml

The file stays on the machine, just leaves the repo.

docs.title: Something went wrong
docs.text: I see Do chezmoi: command not found / not recognized Close and reopen the terminal. VDI: redo the PATH step. Permission denied (publickey) Wrong SSH passphrase, or the key is not on GitHub. Test ssh -T git@github.com (VDI: ssh -T github_vdi). Red error at terminal start chezmoi apply -v again. Still red → reference troubleshooting. It installed something I don't want here Remove that profile from the program's on: in packages.yaml, uninstall by hand. No idea chezmoi doctor and ask the AI agent.

docs.title: Dotfiles reference
docs.text:
NOTE: First time? Start with the Quick Start. This page explains how it works.

One private repo, Buerostuff/dotfiles, keeps my agent rules, skills, tool settings and program list. On a new machine one command brings everything back - only the parts meant for that profile.

docs.title: 1. Concepts
docs.text:
Term Meaning chezmoi Small tool (single exe) that copies files from a git repo into my home folder. Source dir The repo on disk. VDI: C:\Install\_github\dotfiles. Elsewhere default: ~/.local/share/chezmoi. I edit here. Target The real file in my home folder (e.g. ~/.config/opencode/AGENTS.md). Template (.tmpl) File with {{ if ... }} blocks - content changes per profile / OS. Script (run_...) Script chezmoi runs on apply (install programs, copy settings). Profile Who uses the machine and what it may get. Asked once per machine. OS Detected automatically (windows, darwin, linux). Not a profile. 
 GitHub repo  ── git pull / chezmoi update ──▶  source dir  ── chezmoi apply ──▶  home folder
 (private)    ◀──────── git push ───────────   (the repo)   ◀── chezmoi re-add ──

Only files I explicitly chezmoi add are managed. Everything else is untouched.

docs.title: 2. Profiles
docs.text:
Profile = trust level / purpose. OS is separate and automatic, so there is no "windows-personal" vs "mac-personal" - just rg-personal on any OS.

Profile Machine Idea rg-personal my own laptops / PCs everything rg-semi own use, not fully mine like personal, but no git identity, no SSH rg-vdi company dev VDI (no admin) full work dev setup rg-work company laptop only Lintalist rg-collab shared with a colleague dev tools + shell look, none of my rules rg-public shared / untrusted shell look + core tools only

docs.title: 2.1 Dotfiles per profile
docs.text:
Source of truth: .chezmoidata/dotfiles.yaml.

Dotfile personal semi vdi work collab public Agent rules AGENTS.md ✓ ✓ ✓ (+VDI, IT tickets) Skills (.agents, .claude, opencode) ✓ ✓ ✓ opencode.jsonc ✓ ✓ ✓ .gitconfig (name + email) ✓ ✓ starship.toml ✓ ✓ ✓ ✓ ✓ PowerShell profile ✓ ✓ ✓ ✓ ✓ VS Code keybindings + snippets ✓ ✓ ✓ Lintalist settings + snippets ✓ ✓ ✓ ✓ SSH config (github_vdi, devops) ✓ Windows Terminal settings.json ✓ ✓

Not synced on purpose: VS Code settings.json (holds DB connection passwords), SSH keys.

docs.title: 2.2 Programs per profile
docs.text:
Source of truth: .chezmoidata/packages.yaml.

Program personal semi vdi work collab public Git, PowerShell 7, Starship, ripgrep, VS Code ✓ ✓ ✓ ✓ ✓ chezmoi ✓ ✓ ✓ ✓ ✓ ✓ Cursor, Zed ✓ ✓ ✓ ✓ Node, Bun, Python 3.13, uv, Go, .NET 10, Docker ✓ ✓ ✓ ✓ HeidiSQL, Azure Storage Explorer, WinSCP ✓ ✓ ✓ Obsidian, PDF-XChange ✓ ✓ ✓ Lintalist ✓ ✓ ✓ ✓

docs.title: 3. What is in the repo
docs.text:
dotfiles/
├── .chezmoi.toml.tmpl                    # asks profile, sets sourceDir, runs .ps1 with pwsh
├── .chezmoiignore                        # never-sync list + per-profile / per-OS skips
├── .chezmoidata/
│   ├── dotfiles.yaml                     # dotfile groups → profiles
│   └── packages.yaml                     # programs → profiles (winget / brew / VDI dir)
├── .chezmoiscripts/
│   ├── run_onchange_install-packages.ps1.tmpl       # Windows: winget, or VDI check
│   ├── run_onchange_install-packages.sh.tmpl        # macOS / Linux: brew
│   ├── run_onchange_after_pwsh-profile.ps1.tmpl     # puts pwsh profile in place
│   └── run_onchange_after_lintalist-settings.ps1.tmpl  # copies Lintalist settings
├── README.md                             # not placed in home
├── AppData/Roaming/Code/User/            # VS Code keybindings + snippets
├── dot_config/
│   ├── opencode/  AGENTS.md.tmpl, opencode.jsonc.tmpl, skill/
│   ├── powershell/Microsoft.PowerShell_profile.ps1.tmpl
│   ├── lintalist/ Settings.ini, *.ini, bundles/, local/
│   └── starship.toml
├── dot_agents/skills/...
├── dot_claude/skills/react-doctor/
├── dot_gitconfig
└── dot_ssh/config                        # VDI only, never keys
Repo name Becomes in home dot_config .config x.tmpl x (rendered per profile / OS) .chezmoiscripts/run_onchange_x.ps1.tmpl script, runs when its content changes run_onchange_after_... same, runs after files are placed .chezmoidata/*.yaml data for templates (.packages, .dotfiles)

docs.title: 4.1 Get git + chezmoi
docs.text:
Windows (winget)VDI (no admin)macOS / Linux 
winget install Git.Git twpayne.chezmoi

Download the Windows zip from https://github.com/twpayne/chezmoi/releases, unpack to C:\Install\Programs\chezmoi, then add to the user PATH:

[Environment]::SetEnvironmentVariable('Path',
  [Environment]::GetEnvironmentVariable('Path','User') + ';C:\Install\Programs\chezmoi',
  'User')

New terminal → chezmoi --version.

Install Homebrew (https://brew.sh), then:

brew install git chezmoi

docs.title: 4.2 Pull the repo and pick the profile (HTTPS - no SSH key needed yet)
docs.text:
Windows / macOS / LinuxVDI (repo in C:\Install_github) 
chezmoi init https://github.com/Buerostuff/dotfiles.git

git clone https://github.com/Buerostuff/dotfiles.git C:\Install\_github\dotfiles
chezmoi init --source C:\Install\_github\dotfiles

A browser login opens (Git Credential Manager). chezmoi asks:

Profile: rg-personal / rg-semi / rg-vdi / rg-work / rg-collab / rg-public

Non-interactive shell: add --promptChoice "Profile=rg-vdi".

docs.title: 4.3 Preview, then apply
docs.text:
chezmoi diff      # what would change
chezmoi apply -v  # place files + run scripts (install programs, profile, Lintalist)

docs.title: 4.4 SSH key for this machine
docs.text: See 8. SSH.

docs.title: 4.5 Switch the repo to SSH (optional)
docs.text:
chezmoi cd
git remote set-url origin git@github.com:Buerostuff/dotfiles.git   # VDI: github_vdi:Buerostuff/dotfiles.git
exit

docs.title: 5.1 Ask once - .chezmoi.toml.tmpl
docs.text:
{{- $profile := promptChoiceOnce . "profile" "Profile" (list "rg-personal" "rg-semi" "rg-vdi" "rg-work" "rg-collab" "rg-public") -}}
sourceDir = {{ .chezmoi.sourceDir | quote }}

[data]
  profile = {{ $profile | quote }}

[interpreters.ps1]
  command = "pwsh"
  args = ["-NoLogo", "-NoProfile", "-ExecutionPolicy", "Bypass"]

Show it: chezmoi data. Change it: chezmoi init --prompt, or edit ~/.config/chezmoi/chezmoi.toml.

docs.title: 5.2 Dotfile groups - .chezmoidata/dotfiles.yaml
docs.text:
dotfiles:
  agents:     [rg-personal, rg-semi, rg-vdi]
  gitconfig:  [rg-personal, rg-vdi]
  lintalist:  [rg-personal, rg-semi, rg-vdi, rg-work]
  ssh:        [rg-vdi]
  # ...

To give a profile a dotfile: add the profile to that group. Done.

docs.title: 5.3 Skipping - .chezmoiignore
docs.text:
Each group skips its files when the profile is not listed:

{{ if not (has .profile .dotfiles.gitconfig) }}
.gitconfig
{{ end }}

Plus per-OS skips (AppData/**, Lintalist only on Windows) and the never-sync list. Paths are home paths (.config/...), not repo paths.

docs.title: 5.4 Sections inside one file - AGENTS.md.tmpl
docs.text:
{{ if eq .profile "rg-vdi" -}}
## Corporate DevVDI (no admin rights)
...
{{ end -}}
Section personal / semi vdi Communication, Todo list, Git, Installing software, Env files ✓ ✓ Cloning via github_vdi, .NET on the DevVDI, Corporate DevVDI, IT tickets ✓

docs.title: 5.5 Test another profile without changing this machine
docs.text:
chezmoi managed --include files --override-data '{"profile":"rg-work"}'

'{"profile":"rg-personal"}' | Set-Content $env:TEMP\p.json
chezmoi execute-template --override-data-file $env:TEMP\p.json `
  --file "$(chezmoi source-path)\dot_config\opencode\AGENTS.md.tmpl"

docs.title: 6. Programs
docs.text: Program files are not synced. Only the list is.

docs.title: 6.1 Entry format
docs.text:
- name: VS Code
  winget: Microsoft.VisualStudioCode   # Windows (not VDI)
  brew: visual-studio-code             # macOS / Linux
  cask: true                           # GUI app → brew --cask (macOS only)
  dir: Microsoft VS Code               # VDI: C:\Install\Programs\<dir>
  url: https://code.visualstudio.com/#alt-downloads   # by-hand download
  on: [rg-personal, rg-semi, rg-vdi, rg-collab, rg-public]

docs.title: 6.2 What happens on apply
docs.text:
Scripts re-run only when packages.yaml changes (they embed its hash).

Where Behaviour Windows (not VDI) not found by winget list → winget install --scope user, fallback machine scope. No winget id (Lintalist) → listed "install by hand" if C:\Install\Programs\<dir> is missing. VDI (rg-vdi) never downloads. Lists missing C:\Install\Programs\<dir> with URL. macOS brew install / brew install --cask. No brew id → skipped. Linux brew install for CLI formulas; casks listed "install by hand".

docs.title: 6.3 Add or remove a program
docs.text:
1. winget search <name> / brew search <name> for the ids.
  2. Edit packages.yaml (on: decides who gets it).
  3. chezmoi apply -v.
  4. Commit + push.

docs.title: 7.1 PowerShell profile
docs.text:
Source: dot_config/powershell/Microsoft.PowerShell_profile.ps1.tmpl → ~/.config/powershell/ (the native path on macOS / Linux).

On Windows a script copies it to the real profile:

Profile Copied to Why rg-vdi $PSHOME → C:\Install\Programs\PowerShell\7\Microsoft.PowerShell_profile.ps1 Group policy blocks scripts in Documents ("blocked by software restriction policies"). others $PROFILE (Documents\PowerShell\...) normal place

Content: Starship prompt; on VDI the .NET 10 PATH fix (C:\Install\Programs\dotnet before the system SDK 8); Sync-Dotfiles (9.1).

docs.title: 7.2 Lintalist
docs.text:
Lintalist lives in C:\Install\Programs\lintalist64 - outside home, so chezmoi keeps a copy in ~/.config/lintalist (Settings.ini, AltPaste.ini, LineFeed.ini, multicaret.ini, Sound.ini, bundles/default.txt, local/local.txt).

  • Repo → Lintalist: chezmoi apply copies them into the install folder (only when they changed). Restart Lintalist.
  • Lintalist → repo: automatic via Sync-Dotfiles (see 9.1). New bundles are reported; add them with "check all and sync". By hand: Sync-Dotfiles.

docs.title: 7.3 VS Code
docs.text: Synced: keybindings.json, snippets/. Not settings.json - it holds DB connections with passwords (chezmoi warned on add). Never add it.

docs.title: 7.4 Windows Terminal
docs.text: AppData/Local/Packages/Microsoft.WindowsTerminal_8wekyb3d8bbwe/LocalState/settings.json for rg-personal and rg-vdi. It contains VDI paths (C:\Install\Programs\PowerShell\7\pwsh.exe, start folder C:\Install\_github) - on a personal machine use the same folders or change them there in the repo file.

docs.title: 8. SSH
docs.text:
Keys are never in the repo. Each machine gets its own key, so a lost laptop = delete one key on GitHub. Full key setup: Git SSH Setup.

ssh-keygen -t ed25519 -C "<machine-name>"
Get-Content $HOME\.ssh\id_ed25519.pub | Set-Clipboard

Paste into GitHub → Settings → SSH and GPG keys → New SSH key.

~/.ssh/config is synced only to rg-vdi (github_vdi port-443 alias, VDI key names). Other machines write their own.

ssh -T git@github.com      # elsewhere
ssh -T github_vdi          # VDI (port 22 blocked)

Clone on VDI: git clone github_vdi:<owner>/<repo>.git.

docs.title: 9. Daily use
docs.text:
I want to... Command Start syncing a new file chezmoi add <path> (then add it to a group in dotfiles.yaml + .chezmoiignore) Edit a managed file chezmoi edit <path> then chezmoi apply I edited a plain (non-template) file directly chezmoi re-add See differences chezmoi diff Save to GitHub chezmoi cd → git add <files> → git commit → git push → exit Get changes on another machine chezmoi update (= git pull + apply) Stop syncing a file (keeps it locally) chezmoi forget <path> List managed files chezmoi managed Show profile / OS chezmoi data

NOTE: AGENTS.md, opencode.jsonc and the PowerShell profile are templates. Edit the .tmpl in the repo (or chezmoi edit), then chezmoi apply. Direct edits to the target are overwritten on the next apply.

docs.title: 9.1 Automatic: Sync-Dotfiles
docs.text:
Defined in the PowerShell profile (all profiles). On terminal start it runs in the background, at most once per hour:

Step What 1 Repo must be clean - otherwise it only reports "uncommitted changes" (protects work in progress). 2 Lintalist: copies changed tracked files back from C:\Install\Programs\lintalist64. 3 chezmoi re-add - picks up changes to all tracked plain files (not templates). 4 Secret scan on changed files - hit → nothing committed, file named. 5 Commit only those paths: chore(sync): dotfiles <date> from <machine>. No push. 6 New untracked files in watched folders (watch: in dotfiles.yaml) and new Lintalist bundles → only reported.

The result shows as one yellow line at the next terminal start, e.g.

dotfiles: 2 file(s) committed - push when ready | 1 new untracked: .agents/skills/my-skill - say 'check all and sync'

Run it now by hand: Sync-Dotfiles. Last result: ~/.cache/dotfiles-sync.txt.

docs.title: 9.2 New files: "check all and sync" (with the AI agent)
docs.text:
Say "check all and sync" to the agent. The rule lives in AGENTS.md, so every machine with agent rules knows it.

  1. Agent checks (read-only): chezmoi diff, new files in watched folders (skills, VS Code snippets, Lintalist), unmanaged config of listed programs, installed vs packages.yaml, repo git status, password scan.
  2. Agent asks per group: add or skip, which profiles get it.
  3. Agent adds the picks, chezmoi diff is empty.
  4. Agent shows the diff + commit message → I say yes → commit.
  5. I push.

docs.title: 10. Never sync
docs.text:
• SSH private keys, tokens, passwords
  • VS Code settings.json (DB connection passwords)
  • .env, .env.* files
  • node_modules, caches, program binaries

docs.title: 11. Cheat sheet
docs.text:
# new machine
chezmoi init https://github.com/Buerostuff/dotfiles.git
chezmoi diff
chezmoi apply -v

# daily
chezmoi edit <file>; chezmoi apply
chezmoi update
Sync-Dotfiles                 # commit tracked changes now (no push)
chezmoi cd                    # git push, then exit

# inspect
chezmoi managed
chezmoi data
chezmoi doctor

docs.title: 12. Troubleshooting
docs.text: Problem Fix chezmoi not found Add its folder to user PATH, open a new terminal. init hangs at "Profile?" Non-interactive shell: --promptChoice "Profile=rg-vdi". Profile "blocked by software restriction policies" VDI policy. Use rg-vdi (profile goes to $PSHOME), delete Documents\PowerShell\Microsoft.PowerShell_profile.ps1. chezmoi add warns about a password Do not commit it. Remove from the repo, add the path to .chezmoiignore. Permission denied (publickey) Public key not on GitHub, or wrong host alias. Test with ssh -T .... port 22: Connection timed out Network blocks 22 → use the github_vdi (port 443) alias. Whole file shows as changed in diff Line endings (LF vs CRLF) differ. Keep the target's endings. Script did not run run_onchange runs only when content changes. Force: chezmoi state delete-bucket --bucket=entryState, then chezmoi apply. Template error chezmoi execute-template --file <tmpl> to see the output. Something looks off chezmoi doctor.

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
macOSLinuxWindows 
brew install --cask docker

Or download from docker.com

curl -fsSL https://get.docker.com | sh
sudo usermod -aG docker $USER
# logout and login

# winget
winget install Docker.DockerDesktop

# scoop
scoop install docker

Or download from docker.com

docs.title: Running Docker in VDI Environment
docs.text: In corporate VDI (Virtual Desktop Infrastructure) environments, Docker Desktop may require elevated privileges to run properly.

docs.title: Step 1: Right-click Docker Desktop
docs.text: Right-click the Docker Desktop shortcut and select Run with Administrator Privileges.

docs.title: Step 2: Provide Elevation Reason
docs.text: A Privilege Elevation dialog will appear. Enter a reason (e.g., "Development work") and click Continue.

docs.title: Step 3: Confirmation
docs.text:
You'll see a confirmation that Docker is now running with administrator privileges.

TIP: If Docker fails to start containers or shows permission errors, running with elevated privileges usually resolves these issues in VDI environments.

docs.title: Login to Azure Container Registry
docs.text:
Before pulling images from Azure Container Registry (ACR), you need to authenticate with Azure first.

WARNING: In VDI environments, run these commands in a normal terminal (not elevated). ACR login does not work in terminals started with administrator privileges.

docs.title: Step 1: Login to Azure
docs.text:
az login

Or use device code for remote/VDI sessions:

az login --use-device-code

docs.title: Step 2: Select Subscription
docs.text:
List available subscriptions and select the correct one:

az account list -o table
az account set -s "<subscription-name-or-id>"

docs.title: Step 3: Login to ACR
docs.text: az acr login -n <acr-name>

docs.title: Step 4: Docker Login
docs.text:
docker login <acr-name>.azurecr.io

NOTE: ACR login tokens are valid for 3 hours. Re-run az acr login and docker login if you get authentication errors.

docs.title: Troubleshooting: Docker Login Still Fails
docs.text:
If docker login still doesn't work, edit the Docker config file:

  • Windows: %USERPROFILE%\.docker\config.json
  • macOS/Linux: ~/.docker/config.json

Change credsStore from:

"credsStore": "wincred",

To:

"credsStore": "",

Then retry the docker login command.

docs.title: Custom Install Path (Windows)
docs.text:
Don't double-click the installer. Use command line to specify custom paths.

PowerShellCMD 
# Run as Administrator
cd ~\Downloads
Start-Process -Wait -FilePath ".\Docker Desktop Installer.exe" -ArgumentList "install", "-accept-license", "--installation-dir=D:\Docker", "--wsl-default-data-root=D:\Docker\images"

:: Run as Administrator
cd %USERPROFILE%\Downloads
start /w "" "Docker Desktop Installer.exe" install -accept-license --installation-dir=D:\Docker --wsl-default-data-root=D:\Docker\images

Flags explained:

Flag Purpose -accept-license Auto-accept license agreement --installation-dir=D:\Docker Install Docker app to D:\Docker --wsl-default-data-root=D:\Docker\images Store WSL data & images on D:

NOTE: Without --wsl-default-data-root, images still go to %HOME%\AppData\Local\Docker

docs.title: Clone
docs.text:
SSHHTTPS 
git clone git@github.com:<username>/<repo>.git

NOTE: If you have multiple SSH profiles, replace github.com with your SSH config host (e.g., github_vdi). Check your ~/.ssh/config file.

git clone https://github.com/<username>/<repo>.git

docs.title: Push Existing Local Project to GitHub
docs.text:
If you already have a local project with git init, connect it to GitHub:

SSHHTTPS 
git remote add origin git@github.com:<username>/<repo>.git
git branch -M main
git push -u origin main

NOTE: If you have multiple SSH profiles, replace github.com with your SSH config host (e.g., github_vdi). Check your ~/.ssh/config file.

git remote add origin https://github.com/<username>/<repo>.git
git branch -M main
git push -u origin main

NOTE: Create an empty repository on GitHub first (without README or .gitignore) before pushing.

docs.title: Branch Management
docs.text: Command Description git switch <branch> Switch to an existing branch git switch -c <branch> Create and switch to a new branch git switch - Switch to the previous branch git branch List local branches git branch -a List all branches (local and remote) git branch -d <branch> Delete a branch (safe, checks if merged) git branch -D <branch> Force delete a branch (even if not merged) git branch -m <old> <new> Rename a branch

docs.title: Flags for git switch
docs.text: Flag Description -c Create a new branch and switch to it - Switch to the previously checked out branch --discard-changes Discard local changes when switching

docs.title: Committing
docs.text: Command Description git add . Stage all changes in current directory git add -A Stage all changes (entire repo) git add <file> Stage a specific file git commit -m "message" Commit with a message git status Show working tree status git diff Show unstaged changes

docs.title: One-liner (Add + Commit)
docs.text:
git add -A && git commit -m "Your message here"

Or using PowerShell 5.x (use semicolon):

git add -A; git commit -m "Your message here"

docs.title: Flags for git add
docs.text: Flag Description -A Stage all changes (new, modified, deleted) in entire repo . Stage all changes in current directory and subdirectories -p Interactive staging (choose which hunks to stage) -u Stage only modified and deleted files (not new files)

docs.title: Flags for git commit
docs.text: Flag Description -m "message" Provide commit message inline -a Automatically stage modified files (not new files) -am "message" Combine -a and -m (stage modified + commit) --amend Modify the last commit

docs.title: Flags for git merge
docs.text: Flag Description --no-ff Create a merge commit even for fast-forward --abort Abort the current merge operation --squash Squash all commits into one (no auto-commit)

docs.title: Add SSH Key to GitHub
docs.text:
1. Go to GitHub SSH Settings
  2. Click New SSH key
  3. Give it a title (e.g., "Work Laptop")
  4. Paste your public key
  5. Click Add SSH key

NOTE: See GitHub's official guide: Adding a new SSH key to your GitHub account

docs.title: Why Port 443?
docs.text:
Many corporate firewalls block port 22 (default SSH port). GitHub allows SSH connections over port 443 (HTTPS port) which is usually open.

macOS / LinuxWindows

Edit ~/.ssh/config:

Host github.com
    HostName ssh.github.com
    Port 443
    User git
    IdentityFile ~/.ssh/id_ed25519

Edit C:\Users\<username>\.ssh\config:

Host github.com
    HostName ssh.github.com
    Port 443
    User git
    IdentityFile C:\Users\<username>\.ssh\id_ed25519

docs.title: Test Connection
docs.text:
ssh -T git@github.com

Expected output:

Hi username! You've successfully authenticated, but GitHub does not provide shell access.

docs.title: Multiple Git Profiles
docs.text: If you have multiple GitHub accounts (e.g., personal and work), you can configure separate SSH keys and profiles.

docs.title: Step 1: Generate Separate Keys
docs.text:
# Personal account
ssh-keygen -t ed25519 -C "personal@email.com" -f ~/.ssh/id_ed25519_personal

# Work account
ssh-keygen -t ed25519 -C "work@company.com" -f ~/.ssh/id_ed25519_work

docs.title: Step 2: Add Keys to SSH Agent
docs.text:
macOS / LinuxWindows 
ssh-add ~/.ssh/id_ed25519_personal
ssh-add ~/.ssh/id_ed25519_work

ssh-add $env:USERPROFILE\.ssh\id_ed25519_personal
ssh-add $env:USERPROFILE\.ssh\id_ed25519_work

docs.title: Step 3: Configure SSH Config
docs.text:
Edit ~/.ssh/config (or C:\Users\<username>\.ssh\config on Windows):

# Personal GitHub
Host github.com
    HostName ssh.github.com
    Port 443
    User git
    IdentityFile ~/.ssh/id_ed25519_personal

# Work GitHub (use custom host alias)
Host github_work
    HostName ssh.github.com
    Port 443
    User git
    IdentityFile ~/.ssh/id_ed25519_work

docs.title: Step 4: Add Keys to GitHub Accounts
docs.text:
Add each public key to its respective GitHub account:

  • Personal: Add id_ed25519_personal.pub to your personal GitHub
  • Work: Add id_ed25519_work.pub to your work GitHub

docs.title: Step 5: Clone Using Profile
docs.text:
# Personal (default)
git clone git@github.com:personal-user/repo.git

# Work (use custom host)
git clone git@github_work:work-org/repo.git

docs.title: Step 6: Configure Git User Per Repository
docs.text:
After cloning, set the correct user for each repo:

cd /path/to/work/repo
git config user.name "Your Work Name"
git config user.email "work@company.com"

TIP: For automatic user config based on folder, see Conditional Git Config.

# Check current remote

docs.title: Branch Structure
docs.text:
main
  └── integration
        ├── feature/xyz
        ├── feature/abc
        └── fix/bug-123
Branch Purpose main Production-ready code (stable, tested) integration Staging area where features are merged and tested feature/* Individual work branches for new features fix/* Bug fix branches

docs.title: 1. Start New Work
docs.text:
git switch integration
git pull origin integration
git switch -c feature/my-feature

docs.title: 2. Develop and Commit
docs.text:
git add .
git commit -m "Add feature description"

docs.title: 3. Merge to Integration
docs.text:
git switch integration
git pull origin integration
git merge feature/my-feature
git push origin integration

docs.title: 4. Test
docs.text: docker-compose up --build

docs.title: 5. Release to Production
docs.text:
git switch main
git pull origin main
git merge integration
git push origin main

docs.title: 6. Tag the Release
docs.text:
git tag -a v1.0.0 -m "First production release"
git push origin v1.0.0

docs.title: 7. Cleanup
docs.text: git branch -d feature/my-feature

docs.title: Visual Workflow
docs.text:
feature/xyz → integration → main
     ↓             ↓          ↓
  develop        test     production

docs.title: Best Practices
docs.text:
1. Never work directly on main — always go through integration
  2. Never push to main without testing on integration first
  3. Keep features small and focused — easier to review and merge
  4. Merge early, merge often — small merges are easier than large ones
  5. Pull before merge — always update your branch before merging
  6. Update long-running feature branches — merge integration into your feature branch regularly

docs.title: What Are Tags?
docs.text: Tags are permanent bookmarks to specific commits — used to mark production releases.

docs.title: Why Tags Instead of Branches?
docs.text:
Feature Branch Tag Moves with new commits ✅ Yes ❌ No (stays fixed) Points to latest code ✅ Yes ❌ No Marks a specific release ❌ No ✅ Yes Creates GitHub Releases ❌ No ✅ Yes

Example:

main → [commit C] → [commit B] → [commit A]
                         ↑
                      v1.0.0 (stays here forever)

Even after 100 more commits, v1.0.0 still points to commit B.

docs.title: Version Numbering
docs.text:
v1.0.0 → First release
v1.0.1 → Bug fix (patch)
v1.1.0 → New feature (minor)
v2.0.0 → Breaking changes (major)
Version Part When to Increment Major (v2.0.0) Breaking changes, major rewrites Minor (v1.1.0) New features, backwards compatible Patch (v1.0.1) Bug fixes, small improvements

docs.title: When to Tag
docs.text: Situation Action Code tested & merged to main Create tag v1.0.0 Hotfix deployed Create tag v1.0.1 New feature released Create tag v1.1.0

docs.title: Tag Commands
docs.text:
# Create annotated tag
git tag -a v1.0.0 -m "First production release"

# Push tag to GitHub
git push origin v1.0.0

# List all tags
git tag

# Delete local tag
git tag -d v1.0.0

# Delete remote tag
git push origin --delete v1.0.0

docs.title: Benefits of Tagging
docs.text:
1. Rollback easily — if v1.1.0 breaks, checkout v1.0.0
  2. GitHub Releases — tags become downloadable releases with assets
  3. Track production — always know exactly which code is live
  4. CI/CD triggers — many pipelines auto-deploy when a tag is pushed

TIP: Tag it when it hits production! 🚀

docs.title: Handling Multiple Features
docs.text:
If you need to pause a feature:

# Save current work
git add .
git commit -m "WIP: feature progress"

# Switch to integration, start new feature
git switch integration
git pull origin integration
git switch -c feature/urgent-fix

# When done, go back to original feature
git switch feature/my-feature
git merge integration

docs.title: Resolving Merge Conflicts
docs.text:
When conflicts occur:

  1. Open the conflicted file
  2. Look for conflict markers: 
    <<<<<<< HEAD
(your branch content)
=======
(incoming branch content)
>>>>>>> branch-name
  3. Edit to keep desired content
  4. Delete the markers (<<<<<<<, =======, >>>>>>>)
  5. Save and commit: 
    git add .
git commit -m "Resolve merge conflict"

docs.title: Quick Conflict Resolution Workflow
docs.text:
1. Press /<<< then Enter to find conflict markers
  2. Press dd to delete the marker line
  3. Navigate with j and k to review content
  4. Delete unwanted lines with dd
  5. Delete remaining markers (=======, >>>>>>>)
  6. Press :wq to save and exit

docs.title: Go Setup
docs.text: Installation and development workflow for Go, including Air for live reload.

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
WindowsmacOS 
# winget
winget install GoLang.Go

# scoop
scoop install go

brew install go

docs.title: Air (live reload)
docs.text: Air provides live reload for Go apps during development. Follow these steps to install and use it.

docs.title: 1. Install Air
docs.text:
Windows / PowerShellmacOS / Linux 
go install github.com/air-verse/air@latest

go install github.com/air-verse/air@latest

Or on macOS via Homebrew:

brew install go-air

docs.title: 2. Add Go bin to PATH (Windows)
docs.text:
The air binary is installed to $(go env GOPATH)/bin (typically %USERPROFILE%\go\bin). Add it to your session PATH:

$env:Path += ";" + (go env GOPATH) + "\bin"

NOTE: This only affects the current session. To make it permanent, add the same line to your PowerShell profile, or add %USERPROFILE%\go\bin to your user PATH in Environment Variables (System Properties → Advanced → Environment Variables).

docs.title: 3. Verify PATH
docs.text:
Confirm that Go's bin directory is on your PATH:

$env:Path -split ";"

Check that %USERPROFILE%\go\bin (or the path from (go env GOPATH)\bin) appears in the list.

docs.title: 4. Initialize Air in your backend
docs.text:
Go to the root folder of your backend (where go.mod and your Go code live) and create the Air config:

cd C:\path\to\your\backend
air init

This creates a .air.toml file in the current directory.

docs.title: 5. Run Air
docs.text:
From the same backend root folder, run:

air

Air will build and run your app and reload when you change your code.

TIP: You can customize build and run behavior by editing .air.toml. See the air-verse/air README and air_example.toml in the repo for options.

docs.title: Custom Install Directory (C:\Install\Programs)
docs.text:
To install scoop packages to a custom directory instead of ~\scoop\apps\:

One-time Setup (Run as Administrator):

# 1. Set the global install path environment variable
$env:SCOOP_GLOBAL = 'C:\Install\Programs'
[Environment]::SetEnvironmentVariable('SCOOP_GLOBAL', $env:SCOOP_GLOBAL, 'Machine')

# 2. Restart terminal to apply changes

Install Packages Globally:

# Use -g flag to install to global directory
scoop install make -g

Verify Installation:

# Check install location
scoop which make

# Test
make --version

NOTE: Global installs (-g) go to C:\Install\Programs. Regular installs go to ~\scoop\apps\. PATH is automatically updated by scoop.

docs.title: Windows Terminal + PowerShell Setup
docs.text: When group policy blocks profile.ps1 execution, configure starship directly in Windows Terminal settings.

docs.title: Terminal Settings
docs.text:
Open Windows Terminal → Settings → Profiles → PowerShell → Command line:

pwsh.exe -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -NoExit -Command "Invoke-Expression (&starship init powershell)"

Or for Windows PowerShell (not pwsh):

powershell.exe -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -NoExit -Command "Invoke-Expression (&starship init powershell)"

docs.title: settings.json
docs.text:
Open settings.json (Ctrl+Shift+,) and edit the PowerShell profile:

{
    "profiles": {
        "list": [
            {
                "name": "PowerShell",
                "commandline": "pwsh.exe -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -NoExit -Command \"Invoke-Expression (&starship init powershell)\"",
                "font": {
                    "face": "JetBrainsMono Nerd Font"
                }
            }
        ]
    }
}

Flags explained:

Flag Purpose -ExecutionPolicy Bypass Ignores group policy restriction -NoExit Keeps terminal open after command -Command "..." Runs starship init on startup
